mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below baseline while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, daytime activity stays suppressed and retail footfall falls further over the next four weeks. The mechanism acts through fewer commuting trips and fewer incidental purchases tied to commuting.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT staying below baseline and RESIDENTIAL staying above baseline for most of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rebound in GROCERY_PHARM signals restored errands and cautious out-of-home movement, which spills into nearby retail visits within one to two weeks and lifts RETAIL_REC. The effect should appear once grocery mobility holds above its recent weekly level rather than from a single-week spike.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises at least 5 points above its prior-week value
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 2 weeks after GROCERY_PHARM rises by 5 or more points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS recover strongly at the same time TRANSIT remains weak, discretionary outdoor activity substitutes for indoor shopping and retail stays depressed over the following month. The interaction matters because park visits draw trips away from malls and central retail corridors without restoring commuter demand.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though PARKS stay elevated and TRANSIT stays below baseline throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES drops further below baseline after already being negative, the city is likely entering a tighter restriction regime that reduces shopping trips within one week. Retail mobility should fall next because workplace closures and telework suppress trip chaining and discretionary visits.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -15 points and remains there for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 1 week after WORKPLACES falls below -15 and stays there for 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RESIDENTIAL indicates people are spending more time at home, which reduces spontaneous retail visits with a lag of roughly two to four weeks as habits reset toward home-based consumption. This effect is strongest when residential mobility is elevated for more than one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean after RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline for at least 2 consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM with weak TRANSIT implies localized neighborhood activity rather than regional shopping trips, which lowers retail mobility over the next two weeks. The signal is a short-horizon substitution away from destination shopping toward local errands and outdoor leisure.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises within 2 weeks even though PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both remain elevated while TRANSIT stays below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT recovers faster than WORKPLACES, retail mobility increases because people resume non-work trips and corridor shopping before full office returns. The mechanism should be visible within four weeks and is strongest when transit gains outpace workplace gains by several points.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above WORKPLACES by at least 5 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days after TRANSIT exceeds WORKPLACES by 5 or more points.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week improvement in WORKPLACES followed by a drop in RESIDENTIAL identifies a reopening shift that raises retail activity after a short lag. The retail response should appear within one week if workplace attendance is normalizing and home-staying is falling at the same time.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 1 week after WORKPLACES increases while RESIDENTIAL decreases in the same week.
